title: Responder knowledge curation and rotation compact guide
author: Asha Menon
content:
Purpose
This compact guide describes how responders should curate incident knowledge, execute rotations, run lightweight postmortems, and use standardized customer and status-page templates. It’s intended for primary on-call engineers, secondary responders, incident commanders, and the SRE rotations manager.

Quick summary
- Goal: reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for recurring patterns by 30% over 3 months through better knowledge capture and rotation hygiene.
- Scope: all production incidents that meet alert thresholds for latency, error-rate, or capacity (see SLO thresholds below).
- Owners: on-call (primary), SRE rotations manager (rotation schedule), incident-retrospective lead (postmortem quality).

When to use this doc
- Any multi-person incident (severity P1/P2) longer than 15 minutes.
- Regression patterns detected by automated SLO regression alerts, or repeating alerts from the same service within 7 days.

SLOs and thresholds (reference)
| Service | SLO (p99 latency) | Error-rate target | Alert threshold |
| Redwood-API-gen | 200ms | <0.5% | p99 > 300ms for 5m OR errors > 1% for 1m |
| Embedding-pipeline | 500ms | <1.0% | latency > 900ms for 10m OR 5% queued tokens |

Incident lifecycle (compact)
1) Detect & Notify
   - Pager triggers to #oncall with runbook link. Pager includes runbook id, sample alerts, and top-2 logs.
2) Triage (primary on-call) — first 10m
   - Identify blast radius (service, region, endpoints).
   - Determine owner: 'compute', 'runtime', 'network', or 'customer-config'.
   - Execute immediate mitigations: scale-up, rate-limit, routing fallback. Document each action in incident timeline.
3) Escalate (if >10m unresolved)
   - Contact secondary, then incident commander. Use matrix below.
4) Contain & Restore (15–90m)
   - Follow runbook checklist for the service category. If unknown pattern, run the regression triage checklist.
5) Synthesize knowledge (post-containment)
   - Create a one-paragraph incident summary and one actionable next-step list (5 items max).
6) Postmortem and rotation handoffs (within 72h)
   - Lightweight postmortem must be drafted within 72 hours; owner assigned to finalize within 7 days.

Escalation matrix (compact)
1. Primary on-call (first 10m): attempt containment.
2. Secondary on-call (10–20m): deeper debugging and mitigations.
3. Incident Commander (20–60m): coordinates cross-team actions, customer comms.
4. Platform lead / SRE manager (60m+): exec decision on rollbacks, customer exec notification.

Contact/roles list
- Primary on-call: resolves or escalates.
- Secondary: supports root cause debugging.
- Incident Commander (IC): single point for decisions and customer comms.
- Communications lead: crafts status page and customer messages.
- Postmortem owner: writes final RCA and follow-ups.

Immediate runbook checklist (pattern-based)
Use this checklist when the alert matches a known pattern. If not, shift to regression triage flow.
- Verify monitoring (Grafana /datadog) is accurate.
- Capture a p99/p95/p50 snapshot and recent deployment IDs.
- Check model-serving nodes: `rmi list --service redwood-runtime | grep unhealthy`
- If CPU/GPU saturation: trigger scale policy `infra autoscale --service runtime --up 2`
- If errors spike and correlate with new deploy: roll back to last stable tag `kubectl set image ...`

Regression triage checklist (unknown pattern)
1. Collect evidence: traces, example requests, logs. Use `logs query --svc <svc> --last 30m --filter error`.
2. Identify change vectors: deploys, config changes, infra events, third-party failures.
3. Reproduce locally with traffic replay (if safe) or synthetic requests.
4. If reproducible: implement temporary routing or throttling as containment.
5. Record hypothesis and test results in the timeline.

Postmortem template (lightweight)
- Title: [Service] outage YYYY-MM-DD
- Severity: P1/P2
- Summary (one para): what happened, customer impact, duration
- Timeline (bullet list): ordered actions with timestamps and owners
- Root cause hypothesis: short statement
- Evidence: logs, traces, graphs (links)
- Corrective actions (5 items max): owner + ETA
- Preventative work: larger initiatives for backlog
- Lessons learned (3 bullets): what to change in runbook/alerts/rotations

Postmortem quality bar
- Draft within 72 hours, owner assigned.
- Include at least one reproducible signal and a concrete test to prevent regression.
- Scorecard (0–5): completeness, evidence, actionability, timeline clarity, follow-up closure. Aim >=4.

Rotation hygiene (compact rules)
- Shift length: 1 week primary, 1 week secondary.
- Warm handoff: 30-minute overlap between shifts for the first day of the week.
- Shadowing: new on-call must shadow 2 incidents before independent shifts.
- Knowledge curation: every on-call shift must add/update at least one runbook note or create a ‘playbook snippet’ (max 300 words) describing the incident pattern and mitigation.
- Escalation practice: if the same service has 3 incidents in 14 days, that service goes on a 30-day ‘watch list’ and gets a game-day.

Game day playbook (30–60 minute exercise)
- Objective: validate runbook accuracy and handoffs for a single regression pattern.
- Participants: primary, secondary, IC, communications, product representative.
- Scenario (example): p99 latency spike in Redwood-API-gen after a config rollout.
- Steps:
  1) Inject synthetic alert and start timer.
  2) Primary executes runbook; log actions.
  3) Secondary attempts deeper debugging.
  4) IC practices communications and status update cadence.
  5) After-action (15m): capture gaps, assign remediation tasks.

Status page and customer communication templates
Status page (short form):
- Title: Partial degradation — Redwood-API-gen (region: us-west-2)
- Impact: Customers in us-west-2 may experience elevated request latency and failed streaming responses.
- Current status: Mitigation in progress — traffic routed to fallback model instances.
- ETA: initial mitigation applied; full restoration target 90 minutes.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or on notable progress.

Customer email / CS template (concise):
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood-API-gen in us-west-2 — ongoing mitigation
Hi <CustomerName>,
We’re investigating an issue impacting Redwood-API-gen in us-west-2 that may cause higher latency and occasional failures. Our on-call team has applied a routing mitigation and is continuing work to fully restore service. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you rely on streaming responses for production traffic, please toggle fallback routing (instructions link).
Regards,
Redwood Inference Operations

Communication cadence (IC responsibilities)
- IC posts initial status within 15 minutes.
- Periodic updates every 30 minutes while unresolved.
- Post-incident summary within 72 hours; customer-facing RCA within 7 days for P1 incidents.

Knowledge curation steps (concrete)
1) Immediately after containment: fill the incident summary section in the incident document (one para + five bullets).
2) Within 24 hours: add a short playbook snippet to the service runbook describing the observed signal and the successful mitigation command(s).
3) Within 72 hours: create the lightweight postmortem and link graphs and traces.
4) Before rotation end: ensure follow-ups have owners and estimated completion dates.

Sample timeline entry (format to copy into incident doc)
- 2025-02-10T14:05Z — Alert: p99 latency spike for Redwood-API-gen (primary on-call: linh). Pager sent to #oncall.
- 2025-02-10T14:12Z — Primary investigated, found config rollout at 14:00; scaled runtime +2 nodes (`infra autoscale`).
- 2025-02-10T14:28Z — Secondary engaged. IC declared a P1. Traffic shifted to fallback. Latency improving.
- 2025-02-10T15:20Z — Service restored to SLO. Mitigation confirmed. Created incident summary.

Runbook maintenance & ownership
- Every runbook must list a runbook owner and a last-updated timestamp.
- Owners are responsible for: post-game-day updates, triage notes, and verifying rollback instructions.
- Repo: runbooks are stored in Confluence and mirrored to /docs/runbooks repo nightly.

Escalation and debrief checklist for IC (post-incident)
- Confirm that customer comms were sent and queued for postmortem inclusion.
- Ensure all timeline entries have timestamps and owners.
- Assign postmortem owner and set review meeting (if scorecard <4).
- If the incident is recurring, schedule a game-day within 14 days.

Appendix: common mitigation commands
- Check node health: `nodes get --region us-west-2 --service redwood-runtime`
- Temporary scale up: `infra autoscale --service runtime --up 2 --reason "incident"`
- Rollback last deploy: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-runtime -n production`
- Re-route traffic: `route update --service redwood-api-gen --to fallback-cluster`

Notes and governance
- This guide is intentionally compact to be usable in high-pressure contexts. Teams should expand service-specific steps into their runbooks.
- Every on-call rotation lead should review this guide quarterly and propose changes through the runbook governance process.

End of document
